A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CHORD, with matching core objectives, original experiments and case studies. The text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, allowing new material to be distinguished from revisions and relocations.

before.justification: v2 reports original mathematical-reasoning and tool-use experiments, training-dynamics analyses, ablations and generated-response examples.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds weighting comparisons, expert-source experiments, medical question answering and additional policy-model evaluations.

M1.justification: The hybrid objective and default token weighting phi(p)=p(1-p) remain unchanged. Section 4.3 and Appendix B.1 add an implemented optional variant that updates the mixing coefficient using mu=max(0, threshold-mean_reward), extending the procedure beyond predetermined schedules.

E1.justification: v3 retains the original mathematics, general-reasoning and tool-use coverage, and adds non-verifiable medical question answering on RaR-Medicine with English medical-o1-reasoning expert demonstrations (Appendix B.4). Appendix B.3 also introduces tool-use demonstrations generated by Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct.

E2.justification: LUFFY, whose tool-use results were omitted in v2, is now evaluated on BFCL; SRFT is newly evaluated there (Table 12). Appendix B.2 also adds evaluated comparisons against Entropy Top, Entropy Norm, IS Clip and Focal Loss, substantially expanding the comparison set.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce 400-step mathematical training with synchronization every two updates and 16 rollouts, model-judged medical evaluation, Qwen2.5-3B and Phi-mini-MoE policies, and a 20k-example SFT condition. Appendix A.1 also changes the reported tool-use mu decay from 0.6 to 0 over 20 steps to 0.9 to 0.05 over 30 steps. This establishes a reported setting revision without independently proving a rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds adaptive-threshold sensitivity, alternative token-weighting tests, expert-source sensitivity with qualitative examples, weaker-model and MoE robustness studies, and an investigation of whether scaling SFT eliminates RL's benefit (Appendices B.1-B.3, B.5-B.6 and D.3). The original joint-scheduling analysis and bus-trip case studies are retained in B.7 and E.

E5.justification: Both versions retain avg@32 reporting for AIME and avg@8 for AMC in Appendix A.2. v3 adds no repeated-training-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures. Its new discussion of RL variance does not change statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added, including RaR-Medicine scores of 81.3 for CHORD-phi versus 76.8 for pure RL, and Phi-mini-MoE BFCL scores of 61.6 versus 58.9 (Tables 7 and 9). Original main-table mathematics and CHORD-phi scores remain unchanged. CHORD-mu's BFCL overall score changes from 78.1 to 77.6 and tool-use response length from 130 to 197 (Tables 1-2), alongside the revised reported schedule; these are not established same-setting performance declines.

T1.justification: The principal objectives and assumptions in Equations 1-6 remain unchanged. Appendices B.1-B.2 add limited mathematical definitions for reward-adaptive mixing and alternative token-weighting functions, without adding proofs, theorems or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: identifying shift-readapt-overfit dynamics, introducing dual-control integration of expert data and on-policy learning, and claiming advantages over sequential SFT-then-RL and other baselines. The additional experiments chiefly support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands interpretation and qualifications concerning threshold sensitivity, potentially task-dependent weighting choices, expert style versus expert strength, and weaker models' difficulty absorbing demonstrations. It also discusses continued RL benefits after scaling SFT and explicitly acknowledges configuration dependence and the primarily empirical understanding of pattern shifts (Appendices B and D; Section 6).

D1.justification: v3 supplies technical details for added studies, including weighting cutoffs, synchronization and training budgets, the Qwen3-30B-3A-Instruct medical judge, and 5,000 aligned expert demonstrations for LUFFY/SRFT. Existing software, GPU disclosures and the implementation hyperlink are retained; the new reproducibility statement does not establish changed code availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting medical experiments, focal loss and the MoE evaluation. It explicitly connects loss mixing to scheduled sampling and expands discussion of SimpleMix's dataset-level mixing. The main positioning around instruction-tuned policies versus base-model Zero-RL remains intact.

P1.justification: Most shared exposition is retained. v3 condenses the preliminaries and main related work, adds Section 4.4, expands the conclusion with future directions, and separates appendix setups/prompts from experimental results. Conference headers, author-year citations, acknowledgements and disclosure sections also change the presentation.

P2.justification: v3 adds eight result tables and a medical training-curve figure, revises the tool-use plots, and relocates existing supplemental displays. The manuscript also adopts the ICLR layout, changing title treatment, headers, text width, typography and placement of figures and tables. The framework diagram and many original plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens the evidence behind CHORD: alternative-weighting and expert-source studies test previously limited aspects of its rationale, while actual LUFFY and SRFT tool-use comparisons address an important comparison gap. Medical and additional-model experiments broaden the empirical support, and explicit qualifications better delimit the conclusions. These gains outweigh the remaining lack of training-run uncertainty and the insufficiently specified SFT-scaling results in Appendix D.3.
